extraction.document_summary: Great Eastern Cares Term Plan is an affordable term life insurance product focused on providing basic protection for death and terminal illness. The brochure states it is offered exclusively through selected charities and non-profit organisations, and is designed to help dependants with financial support in the event of the life assured’s demise. Cover can be chosen from S$100,000 to S$300,000, and policy terms are selectable either “up to age 85” or “up to age 100”. The plan pays a lump sum for covered events; for example, a S$200,000 coverage with a policy term up to age 100 pays S$200,000 as a lump sum if death occurs (illustration). It is stated to have no savings/investment feature, so there is no cash value if terminated early.
quality_notes: The brochure provides high-level product features (coverage range, term up to age 85/100, lump-sum payout) but does not include detailed underwriting rules, exact benefit definitions for terminal illness, exclusions list, grace period, or free-look period.
Some figures are presented as marketing/illustration (e.g., “S$120 a year” and the example premium/payout) without confirming guaranteed limits or full rate tables.

policies.quick_summary: Affordable term life insurance with basic protection against death and terminal illness, with coverage chosen from S$100,000 to S$300,000 and term options up to age 85 or up to age 100; pays a lump sum for covered events. Offered via selected charities and non-profit organisations; no savings/investment feature and no cash value if terminated early (per brochure). Their example shows S$200,000 coverage paying a S$200,000 lump sum on death during the term (illustration). Additionally stated as protected up to SDIC limits and subject to policy contract terms/exclusions (not provided). \n"All ages specified refer to age next birthday."

important_caveats: As stated, the product has no savings or investment feature, so there is no cash value if the policy ends or is terminated prematurely.
The brochure notes that terms, conditions and exclusions are specified in the policy contract.
